summary: Edward Capps studied at Illinois College, Yale, Berlin, Munich, and Halle-Wittenberg. He held academic posts at Illinois College (1887–1888), Yale University (1890–1907), and Princeton University (1907–1936).
Active in Indology and history and archaeology, Edward Clive Bayley studied at the East India Company College (Haileybury) around 1840–1842 before joining the Indian Civil Service in 1842.

Scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology Edward Conze studied at Tübingen, Heidelberg, Kiel, Hamburg, Bonn, and Cologne (Ph.D.), under teachers including Max Walleser and Max Scheler. He held posts at London, Wisconsin-Madison, Washington, UC Berkeley, and Lancaster.

Edward Delavan Perry was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He earned degrees from Columbia University (A.B.) and the University of Tübingen (Dr. phil.) and served as Jay Professor at Columbia University from 1891 to 1931.

Working in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and history/archaeology, Edward Denison Ross studied at UCL and under Theodor Nöldeke at Strasbourg. He served as Chair of Persian at UCL, Principal of Aliah University, and Director of SOAS (1916–1937).

Indologist and linguist Edward Elbridge Salisbury studied at Yale and in Europe under Woolsey, Burnouf, Silvestre de Sacy, Garcin de Tassy, Bopp, and Lassen. He was professor at Yale (1841–1854) and later served as President of the American Oriental Society.
Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who completed his doctoral studies under Roderick S. Bucknell. He held a post at the University of Sydney.

Linguist and Tibetologist Edward Garrett earned his Ph.D. at UCLA under Carson Schütze and Dominique Sportiche, later mentored by Anna Szabolcsi. He worked as a research assistant at UCLA (1996–2000) and faculty research assistant at the University of Virginia (2000–2001).

Edward Granville Browne studied at Newcastle, Cambridge, and St Bartholomew's, learning from William Wright and E. B. Cowell. Working in Iranian studies and religious studies, he held Cambridge posts as lecturer in Persian (from 1888) and Adams Professor of Arabic (from 1902).

Sinologist Edward H. Schafer studied at UCLA, UC Berkeley, the University of Hawaiʻi, and Harvard. He served as a professor in the Department of Oriental Languages at UC Berkeley from around 1947 to 1984 and as president of the American Oriental Society.

Edward Hamilton Johnston studied at New College, Oxford, under Arthur Anthony Macdonell. Active in Indology and Buddhist studies, he served in the Indian Civil Service (1908–1924) before becoming a professor at the University of Oxford (1937–1942).

Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar Edward Joseph Thomas earned a master's at the University of St Andrews under John Burnet and studied at Cambridge. He was a professor and Dean of the Oriental Languages Department at the University of Cambridge (1909–1950).

Philosopher Edward S. Casey studied at Yale, Northwestern (Ph.D.), and the Sorbonne under Paul Ricœur. He taught at UC Santa Barbara, Yale, and Stony Brook University, where he served as Dean of the Faculty of Philosophy.

Edward Said studied at Princeton University and Harvard University. A scholar of philosophy and literature, he held a long-standing post in English and Comparative Literature at Columbia University from approximately 1963 until 2003.

Linguist Edward Sapir studied at Columbia University under Wilhelm Wundt and Franz Boas. He served as Chief of the Division of Anthropology at the Geological Survey of Canada (1910–1925) and taught at the University of Chicago and Yale University.

Edward Upham was a scholar in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He was a member of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland (~1824–1834) and a fellow of the Society of Antiquaries of London (~1826–1834).

Indologist and linguist Edward Vernon Arnold studied at the University of Cambridge and at the University of Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth. He was a fellow at Trinity College, Cambridge, and served as a professor at Bangor University from 1884 to 1924.

Indologist and linguist Edward Washburn Hopkins studied at Columbia and Leipzig (Ph.D.) under Albrecht Weber and Ernst Windisch. He taught at Columbia, served as professor at Bryn Mawr (1885–1895), and succeeded William Dwight Whitney as professor at Yale (1895–1926).

Edward Winslow Bastian, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studied at Banaras Hindu University and earned his Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, also studying under Lobsang Tenzin, Geshe Lobsang, and Geshe Lobsang Donyo.

Edwin Arnold, active in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology, studied at King's College London and Oxford. He taught at King Edward's School, served as Principal of Deccan College (1856), and was a visiting lecturer at Keio University.
